# Recorded output of real Btrfs tools

Every file here is the verbatim stdout+stderr of one real command, run against a real Btrfs
filesystem on `btrfs-progs v6.16` on Linux 7.0. The first line of each file is the command; the
last is `[exit <status>]`.

They exist because spec v0.6 §54.4 asks for real Btrfs where the environment permits, and because
§14.3 — snapshots are not recursive across nested subvolumes — is a fact about the filesystem that
a hand-written fixture can very easily get wrong in the direction that loses data.

Regenerated by `scripts/fs-fixtures.sh`, which builds the filesystem from nothing in a disposable
container. Do not hand-edit a file here.

The layout the fixtures were taken against:

```text
subvolid=5   /                 the top level
  256        @                 mounted at /mnt/root
  257        @home             mounted at /mnt/root/home
  258        @var              mounted at /mnt/root/var
  259        @snapshots
  260        @var/lib-app      NESTED inside @var, 4 MiB of data
```

plus, inside `@var`, a plain directory `plain-dir`, and inside `@`, a plain directory named
`looks-like-a-subvol` — Appendix B.9's trap, so a test can prove that a subdirectory named like a
subvolume is not evidence of one.

The two files to read first are `nested-live.txt` and `nested-in-snapshot.txt`. The live `lib-app`
has a `state` directory in it; the same path inside a read-only snapshot of its parent `@var` is
**empty**. That is §14.3, demonstrated rather than asserted, and it is the whole reason the Btrfs
provider creates a separate recovery asset per required subvolume.
